title: Periodicity
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: Why does atomic radius get smaller across a period?
How does electronegativity change when you go down a group?
Can you explain the trend for ionization energy?

explain.say: Today we will look at periodic trends in the periodic table.
First we explore the trend in atomic radius across a period.

draw.text: Atomic Radius: Decreases L to R

explain.say: Next we look at electronegativity across a period.
Then we examine ionization energy down a group.

draw.text: Ionization Energy: Decreases Top to Bottom

explain.say: In general atomic radius decreases across a period.
Electronegativity generally increases across a period.

faq.q: Why does atomic radius get smaller across a period?
faq.a: As you move across a period, the number of protons increases. This stronger positive charge pulls the electrons in the same shell closer to the nucleus.
asks: What causes the decrease in size across a row?
Why is the radius smaller on the right side?

faq.q: Does electronegativity always increase down a group?
faq.a: No, electronegativity generally decreases down a group. The outer electrons are further from the nucleus, making them less tightly held.
asks: Is EN related to distance from the nucleus?
Why does it get smaller going down?

faq.q: What is the main factor affecting these trends?
faq.a: The main factor is the effective nuclear charge. This is the net positive charge felt by the outer electrons.
asks: Does nuclear charge matter for trends?
How does the number of shells affect size?

faq.a: They are general trends, but exceptions can occur due to electron configuration stability. For example, Group 2 elements are sometimes exceptions.
asks: Are there exceptions to these rules?
When can the trends break down?

faq.q: How does ionization energy relate to atomic radius?
faq.a: Smaller atoms generally have higher ionization energies because the valence electrons are held more tightly by the nucleus.
asks: Is there a link between size and IE?
Does small size mean high IE?

facts: Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right across a period.
Electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period.
Ionization energy generally decreases from top to bottom in a group.
The effective nuclear charge increases across a period.

quiz.say: Which element has the smallest atomic radius: Sodium, Magnesium, or Aluminum?
quiz.show: Na vs Mg vs Al Radius
quiz.why: Across a period, the increasing nuclear charge pulls the electron cloud closer, making the atom smaller.

wrong.0: The correct answer is Aluminum because it is furthest right among the three, experiencing the greatest effective nuclear charge.
wrong.2: Sodium is on the far left, where the nuclear pull is weakest, resulting in the largest radius.
wrong.3: Magnesium is in the middle, but Aluminum is further right, experiencing a stronger pull.

quiz.say: Which trend is expected for electronegativity when moving from top to bottom in a group?
quiz.why: As you move down a group, the valence electrons are in higher energy levels, further from the nucleus, and are thus less attracted.

wrong.0: The size change across periods means the pull on electrons is not constant.
wrong.1: While complex, the general trend is a steady decrease due to increasing principal quantum number.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the increasing number of electron shells increases the distance from the nucleus.

quiz.say: If an atom has a very high ionization energy, what can you predict about its atomic radius?
quiz.why: Tightly held electrons, which require more energy to remove, are usually found in smaller atoms.

wrong.0: While group matters, the immediate relationship between high IE and small size is more direct.
wrong.2: Large atoms have loosely held outer electrons, making them easier to remove.
wrong.3: There is a strong correlation; high IE implies a strong attraction to the nucleus.
